method.selection: All @[goal] in tracked Lean; all theorem/lemma/abbrev/def in Solidity/Theorems.lean; top 30 public theorems by distinct direct importers of their defining module, ties path then line. This is module exposure, not declaration usage. Includes examples explicitly.
method.generated: Roots, Corpus, AxiomPins, marked chain/agreement and other marked generation separated. Chain/agreement without markers is an explicit unresolved bucket, never called handwritten. Selected declaration files have no generation marker; no theorem strength verdict depends on generated counts. provenance.py traces known root/corpus/vector producers, including the explicit handwritten Basic/Imported corpus exceptions, and distinguishes chain-generator source uses from expanded proof terms. Historical authorship of untraced files remains unknown; no scale/effort verdict uses that unknown bucket.
method.parsing: Source-level, not elaborated. Premises column is explicit binders; arrows remain in conclusion. Context preserves open/variable commands, including commands from earlier ended sections; consult source for exact scope. No proof rechecked.
method.ratios: calibrate.py compares complete public compiler endpoint declaration code (statement plus proof) and matched finite scenario input counts in the pinned solc snapshot; it never measures headers alone or treats source size as transitive proof effort. The user clarification to H243 requires a nearest external compiler theorem search before non-comparability. similarity.py searches 11 pinned compiler/verification files, records inspected candidates, pairs similar propositions while stating differences, and retains null only with a row-specific reason. Declaration size never measures transitive proof effort.

references.statement:
Theorem compile_semantics:
   precondition interp s env cfg ec prog
 ⇒
   ¬semantics_determ s env prog Fail ⇒
   semantics_determ s env prog
      (semantics ec s.ffi s.ptr_eq_oracle (SND (compile cfg prog)))
references.status: measured pinned source excerpt; source not compiled
references.comparison: A verified pass: non-Fail source semantics and explicit precondition imply equality of source and compiled flat semantics; not a Solidity or full-backend theorem.
references.theorem_source:
Theorem compile_semantics:
   precondition interp s env cfg ec prog
 ⇒
   ¬semantics_determ s env prog Fail ⇒
   semantics_determ s env prog
      (semantics ec s.ffi s.ptr_eq_oracle (SND (compile cfg prog)))
Proof
  rw [compile_def]
  \\ pairarg_tac \\ fs []
  \\ fs [precondition_def]
  \\ imp_res_tac compile_prog_semantics \\ rfs []
  \\ ‘c'.pattern_cfg = cfg.pattern_cfg’
    by (fs [compile_prog_def] \\ rpt (pairarg_tac \\ fs []) \\ rveq \\ fs [])
  \\ ‘semantics ec1 s.ffi s.ptr_eq_oracle p' ≠ Fail’ by (strip_tac \\ fs [])
  \\ drule_all compile_flat_correct
  \\ disch_then (assume_tac o GSYM) \\ fs []
QED

reference_calibration.conclusion: The small checked compiler facade is an outlier against the CakeML facade because compact Input/Agrees contracts hide detail that the reference facade exposes; both sides delegate. Other measured facade and finite-case ratios are within 3x. Additional similar-theorem ratios include small fixed local computations and delegating calculus facades versus general external theorems. Their recorded outliers reflect different generality or proof packaging, not measured transitive proof effort. Semantic compiler weaknesses are assessed from permitted behaviours, not inferred from these sizes.
